adp.mode.bridgePlain: bridge (no handshake; this version needs no guards)
adp.caps.title: Features with plugins — state and next step
adp.caps.intro: One feature per row: does it work now, in which mode, and what to do if something is missing. You can work without plugins — the 'Without plugin' column shows what stays available.
adp.caps.convertersNone: PNG/PDF from the engine SVG: no working local converter
adp.caps.loadFailed: The adapter state cannot be loaded right now.
adp.caps.why.title: What do the states mean?
adp.caps.why.body: 'working': the plugin connects directly with its current version. 'old version (bridge)': the workbench reads the plugin's old output and corrects its known bugs (H1–H7) with its own guards — the result is reliable. 'installed but unusable': a dependency is missing; the next-step column says exactly what to install. 'not installed': the feature works without the plugin, using the fallback.
adp.fig.title: Export a figure
adp.fig.intro: Publication figure from a committed run. Numbers are the engine's finished texts; after export the workbench compares them letter by letter with the figure.
adp.fig.staleNote: STALE run: the data table changed since this run (X001). The figure shows the run's numbers — re-run the analysis before submitting.
adp.fig.noRuns: No committed run yet. On the Analysis tab use 'Commit' to create one — figures are only exported from committed runs so that every number is traceable.
adp.fig.r.engineNote: labels in the chosen language (Hungarian or English), layered SVG, true minus sign; plus the workbench's own number check
adp.fig.svgAlways: the SVG master is always produced
adp.fig.stemBad: The file name must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
adp.fig.overwriteBody: A figure with this name already exists: {list}. Overwriting replaces the old files (the activity log keeps their hashes).
adp.fig.previewNote: For a quick look only: no label check and no number fidelity check. Submit the export above (SVG/PDF).
adp.fig.previewFailed: The preview failed: the browser could not draw the SVG.
adp.fig.previewNeedsSvg: Export the figure (SVG) first to preview it.
adp.qc.title: Result and quality check
adp.qc.issues: Needs review — see the marked rows
adp.qc.numbers: Number fidelity (workbench re-check): {matched}/{checked} engine texts verbatim in the figure
adp.qc.numbersNone: No checkable engine text for this figure.
adp.qc.editable: Editable: {n} labels are real text, {outlined} outlined
adp.qc.notEditable: NOT editable: {outlined} label groups outlined to paths
adp.qc.fontStack: font fallback stack (looks the same on other machines)
adp.qc.noFontStack: a single font — may differ on other machines
adp.qc.ffDown: The figure-forge audit does not run now: {msg}
adp.qc.why.title: Why does number fidelity matter?
adp.qc.why.body: Every number in the figure comes from the engine's finished text (e.g. '0.49 [0.33; 0.73]'). After export the workbench looks for each of them in the figure, letter by letter (treating minus-sign variants as equal). The green badge is given only when none is missing — so manuscript and figure cannot disagree.
adp.comp.title: PRISMA numbers from the composer
adp.comp.intro: If you screen with the composer plugin, the workbench reads the PRISMA numbers from there — read only: the screening decisions stay in the composer.
adp.comp.h7: The workbench calls the composer scripts with its own Python interpreter (their first line points to another machine — H7) and never writes the composer state. If the composer is saving, reading is retried three times.
adp.comp.outdir: Output folder (where collect/prisma work, with the prisma/ subfolder)
adp.comp.projectBad: The project name must start with a letter or digit; only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
adp.comp.refreshed: PRISMA numbers refreshed from the composer
adp.comp.confirmBody: The PRISMA numbers were entered manually. Composer mode overwrites them (the activity log keeps the previous version's hash). Continue?
adp.comp.toManualBody: Leaving composer mode for manual numbers needs a reason (logged as a decision). Use the 'Manual override with reason' button on the PRISMA screen.
adp.comp.notYet: Not refreshed from the composer yet.
adp.comp.cantRefresh: Refresh is not possible right now:
adp.comp.why.title: What does 'Refresh from the composer' do?
adp.comp.why.body: It runs the composer export (prisma export --format flow-json) into a temporary folder, maps the numbers to the PRISMA 2020 boxes (the composer's 'included' is the number of included REPORTS, J), checks them with the engine, then writes 02_szures/prisma_flow.json. The number of included studies (I) comes from studies.json.
adp.val.title: Cross-check with the validator plugin
adp.val.notOfficial: NOT the official flowchart result — the judgement is yours.
adp.val.gradeUnreliable: The validator's GRADE certainty is unreliable here — the engine computes the certainty.
adp.val.unresolved: Unresolved: publication bias 'suspected' — choose 0 or −1, with a reason.
adp.val.down: The validator is not available now: {msg}
adp.val.cmp.title: Comparison with the engine check
adp.val.cmp.compWhy: The validator counts its own item list; the engine count is the one that counts.
adp.val.cmp.ruleWhy: The validator's simplified conservative rule (any unfavourable answer sets the worst level) is not the engine's flowchart rule; neither is an official result — the judgement is yours.
adp.val.cmp.provisional: The validator's result is provisional (missing or unsendable answers).
adp.val.cmp.nosWhy: Validator 1.0.0 scores 'Partial yes' as 1 star on every item.
adp.val.cmp.unexplained: The reason for the difference is unknown — review the answers; the engine's result counts.
adp.val.completenessSent: Items sent to the validator: {text} — not comparable with the engine's completeness (see the guards)
